# 1D ring grid with wrap-around motion and noisy sensor
N = 10
belief = np.ones(N) / N

# Transition: move +1 with prob 0.8, stay with 0.2
def predict(b):
    p = np.zeros_like(b)
    for i in range(N):
        p[(i+1) % N] += 0.8 * b[i]
        p[i] += 0.2 * b[i]
    return p

# Observation: sensor reports landmark at positions {3,7}; correct with 0.7
landmarks = {3,7}
def likelihood(z, i):
    has = (i in landmarks)
    return 0.7 if (z and has) or ((not z) and (not has)) else 0.3

def update(prior, z):
    unnorm = np.array([likelihood(z, i)*prior[i] for i in range(N)])
    return unnorm / unnorm.sum()

# Perform one predict-update step
belief = predict(belief)
belief = update(belief, z=True)
print("Belief sums to:", belief.sum())
print("Argmax state:", np.argmax(belief))
description: You can follow motion redistribution and a landmark observation.

steps.description: You start uniform over ten ring positions. predict sends 0.8 of each position's mass forward with wraparound and keeps 0.2 in place.
Positions 3 and 7 contain landmarks. likelihood assigns 0.7 when the observation agrees with landmark presence and 0.3 otherwise.

steps.answer: That division normalizes the observation-weighted masses into a probability distribution.
